profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: The OCA places the Tolga icon’s traditional appearance near Yaroslavl in 1314 and connects it with Bishop Prochorus.
overview.reason: Necessary concise summary of the identified published account; its modern English prose is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: The selected nineteenth-century copy shows Mary and the Child inclining their faces toward each other. Its object date belongs to the copy; it is not presented as the 1314 image from the foundation story.

blocks.text: The published account describes a nocturnal light, a bridge across the river, and the bishop finding an icon. His forgotten staff leads companions back to the place the next morning. The story then relates the construction of a church and the later monastery. The luminous appearance and extraordinary building episode are the source’s traditional narrative.
